pr_title: Ensure homekit_controller recieves zeroconf c# updates
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
    
If an integration has a homekit config flow step
homekit_controller would not see updates for
devices that were paired with it and would not
rescan for changes.

Revision: We only send updates to homekit_controller if the
device is already paired.

Hey there @robbiet480, @Kane610, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with a integration (`zeroconf`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L470) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hey there @Jc2k, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with a integration (`homekit_controller`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L174) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@bdraco ! that was quick. Thanks a lot. It would have been ages before I had the time to put a PR together.

I think when I've talked about this with HA devs before the sticking point was that it's fine for homekit_controller to get the c# updates always but it shouldn't offer a discovery of its own if a native integration has intercepted its zeroconf record. So homekit_controller would also need to apply the tests that `handle_homekit` does.

> @bdraco ! that was quick. Thanks a lot. It would have been ages before I had the time to put a PR together.
> 
> I think when I've talked about this with HA devs before the sticking point was that it's fine for homekit_controller to get the c# updates always but it shouldn't offer a discovery of its own if a native integration has intercepted its zeroconf record. So homekit_controller would also need to apply the tests that `handle_homekit` does.

@Jc2k 

I thought about adding the check in `zeroconf` to not offer discovery in that case, but I think its better to let the user choose if they want to integrate via homekit_controller (local) or the device's api (usually cloud).  If they have already paired it via homekit it is not going to show up so it shouldn't impact most users.

When I think about this from a brand perspective, Home Assistant's tag line is "Open source home automation that puts local control and privacy first."  It makes sense to me to always offer the `homekit_controller` option as seems inline with product vision.    

Additionally, the recent `myq` api changed and everything is broken incident is another reminder that users may have a better experience pairing via `homekit_controller` instead of the cloud api.

The above is just my opinion though so if the direction is to add the check, I can modify this PR to accomplish that.

I totally agree with you everything you have said, and have made similar arguments in the past myself. But I think the core devs opinion was that an integration that knows about only device X will always work better for device X than one that speaks a generic protocol. I can see their point - homekit_controller has to support loads of differing homekit stacks and we've seen how varied they are at following the spec. Things like supporting `false` as a bool value but not `true` or not supporting spaces in JSON. When we've solved those bugs for a new family of devices it works great. But I do still worry about giving users a poor onboarding experience.

The biggest issue I have is one of discoverability. If you are privacy minded or prefer non cloud solutions for stability and longevity but don't know about HomeKit then you are unlikely to find out about homekit_controller. And there are some devices where we can offer push based motion sensors and the native integration can't. So you might be missing out on capabilities too.

The compromise that @balloob suggested a while back was to offer a choice if the user was in "Advanced" mode in the UI. But i'm not sure what that would look like.

I would love to see people using Homekit Controller over cloud options. If there is both a homekit and a local device specific integration, I would say the device specific one wins. But before we can even start to implement such things…

We need to educate users what Homekit Controller is. Users don't understand that controlling their devices via Homekit is an option without owning an Apple product. Caused complains. Lots of issues how to get rid of Homekit controller discoveries 🙄 It's what caused us to introduce unique IDs and ignoring flows. 

I think that in a perfect world, we would be able to show a UI that groups the two discoveries and has a link to "What is Homekit Controller and why I should care".

@Jc2k @balloob Adjusted so only devices that are already paired get sent to `homekit_controller` This avoids the second discovery via `homekit_controller` if another integration claims it but still gets homekit controller the updates it needs.

Edit:  The point about the user being confused about multiple ways to integrate is well taken.   Ideally the UI could ask them how they want to integrate and give them some information on local vs cloud since we know the integration method from the config flow.   That’s for another day though and likely not really worth it until there are more integrations that can be discovered via HomeKit

@balloob thanks for clarifying! The constant distress from the people that thought Apple was going to take over their network or something weird, whilst simultaneously relying on not private not local synchronous polling based integrations was quite taxing! I think we are pretty aligned on how it should work long term, now if only I had a few more days in a week :-)

@bdraco Nice. That will probably get most occurrences. Only edge case I can think of is if it is paired but not with HA (or a different HA). Personally I have done both but mostly for dev environment reasons. Only other option I can think of is to make the model matching code separate from homekit_handle and reuse it from homekit controllers config flow. But maybe too much coupling in that approach.

> @bdraco Nice. That will probably get most occurrences. Only edge case I can think of is if it is paired but not with HA (or a different HA). Personally I have done both but mostly for dev environment reasons. Only other option I can think of is to make the model matching code separate from homekit_handle and reuse it from homekit controllers config flow. But maybe too much coupling in that approach.

I wasn't clear if the edge case was that it will show up in discovery a second time or if `homekit_controller` won't see the `c#` update?

It looks like there is already code in `homekit_controller` to guard against offering to pair if its paired elsewhere.
```
        if paired:
            # Device is paired but not to us - ignore it
            _LOGGER.debug("HomeKit device %s ignored as already paired", hkid)
            return self.async_abort(reason="already_paired")
```
Ah, I had tunnel vision and forgot that homekit_controller would filter it back out. Then yep, this works great.

Hey there @michaelarnauts, @bdraco, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`tado`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L397) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hey there @Jc2k, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`homekit_controller`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L174) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Wow, that's a weird one. Tado have one of the more problematic HomeKit implementations, though. We are going to need to get into a lot more detail to resolve this. At the moment without any exceptions or errors to go on i'm going to try and rule out some basics.

Do you seen any errors in the log?

Can you attach your `configuration/.storage/homekit_controller-entity-map`? This is a blob of JSON as returned by the device itself, and if your TRV's don't appear in that file it means HomeKit doesn't know about them. Or didn't when this file was generated. This could mean that they need re-pairing with the Tado bridge, which isn't something you can do through HomeKit.

The next possibility is a bit technical but I need to sound it out so here goes. Maybe when you paired with Tado your bridge hadn't rediscovered all the TRV's yet. But it published its entity map data with just the bridge in. That's when you paired and HA cached the entity map it was at this stage with some devices missing. Then over the next half hour it found the TRV's and updated the data on the bridge and announced this change by increment a field called `c#` in zeroconf, in line with the HomeKit spec. `homekit_controller` has some code to handle this case, but it's not exercised very often so maybe it has a bug.

But in addition, because the `tado` integration itself recently got a config flow this will almost certainly have broken `homekit_controller`'s ability to monitor the `c#` field. A recentish change to Home Assistant means that native integrations are intercepting HomeKit related zeroconf messages. So homekit_controller never gets a change to refresh the data in the entity map. In this case, `tado` does indeed have such a config flow so this could be happening here.

I'm not sure how to prove that theory. You could try resetting the Tado and then waiting an hour before pairing it with Home Assistant. If you are comfortable editing code I could try talking you through disabling the Tado zeroconf stuff to see if it helps.

Hi,
I attach the file you requested (i think no tvr are present).
[homekit_controller-entity-map.zip](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/4616490/homekit_controller-entity-map.zip)
I don't notice anything strange in the logs (if you want me to activate some logs in particular, ask me and i do it).
If possible I would prefer not to reset the whole system as all devices are correctly coupled with the bridge (i see them in tado site).
What I just did was reset the pairing and I'll try to re-run it tonight.
As for code changes, I can try to follow your directions.

Thanks,
R

Cheers for that. They weren't present in the HomeKit protocol when you paired, and based on you saying they **are** visible in the Tado site it's looking like it is the other Home Assistant integration for your device intercepting the zeroconf announcements meant for homekit_controller.

Let me know how you get on tonight.

I guess another thing you could also seperately try is just deleting the `homekit_controller-entity-map` file and restarting HA. If it then found everything that would prove that `homekit_controller` can't see the c# changes any more so was operating off stale data. 

I'm not sure what shape this proper fix will take. The relevant code doesn't belong to homekit_controller, its in the `zeroconf` integration. In an ideal world zeroconf would:

 * Wait for a new zeroconf event
 * If its a HAP event, see if there is an existing homekit_controller pairing and route it there
 * If a new device with a native integration route it there
    * Optionally if homekit_controller is "better" (not cloud based, push based, async vs sync, gold vs silver, etc), let advanced users pick to use homekit_controller anyway. 
 * Otherwise route it to homekit_controller discovery as usual

But there isn't really a nice way to do that when the logic would be split between 2 integrations.

i try to re-pair bridge after 2 hours.
Now the map-file not contain tvr entities.

It still doesn't contain the tvr entities? Ok. After it has been paired for a while (and after confirming everything is visible in cloud) can you delete the the map file then restart HA. That will force it to fetch a fresh copy. Did that change anything?

here the tado home page screen:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22059192/81733835-e9fc8d00-9492-11ea-8006-cb4b30f0aa1f.png)
 i have deleted the map file and reboot.
7 TVR and 1 Thermostat  are present and entities appear in HA!!
Honestly i do not remember if i have to see 5 tvr and 1 thermosat (not the two in the same room of thermostat) or 7 valves and 1 thermostat.

That's very good news! Based on this and the other things you have said it does sound very much seem like it is related to the `zeroconf` stuff I mentioned. @bdraco has very kindly put together a PR with a fix (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/35545) so it should work automatically again in future.

In the meantime you should be good to go now that the map file has been updated manually. Let me know if you have any other questions.

I think so.
Thanks a lot. Is it normal to see all valves even if twovof them are in the same room.of thermostat?
This closed automagically upon merge of the PR so reopening

@robons17 it's really up to Tado and how they implemented it. In theory each valve could have its own target temperature and so appear as a seperate valve. But there is nothing in the HomeKit protocol to say Tado couldn't make it so that the 2 TRV's with the thermostat are merged into a single entity either. I'd be happy to inspect your map file if you weren't happy with it, but we are at the mercy of their implementation. If you are seeing a seperate entity for every valve then that's "normal" according to them for sure.

@Jc2k thanks a lot.
Here my new map file:
[homekit_controller-entity-map.zip](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/4618232/homekit_controller-entity-map.zip)
so for me it's ok in this way. For example i can make an  automation to set valve temperature setting thermostat temperature. I test that if i change thermostat target temperature after a while also TVR are set to that temperautre.
So I think i create an automation to sync this temperature avoiding that heating turn on with all valve in closed position.
Thanks
R

So it seems like everything seems to be working as expected by Tado. I count 9 accessories. 7 are "Smart Radiator Thermostat". They have 3 services. "accessory-information" - its name and model and things like that, the "thermostat" service and a custom tado specific service thats hidden from the UI. And I can see 1 "Smart Thermostat". Again, same 3 services. The 9th "accessory" is the bridge itself, which doesn't do anything but still counts as an accessory.
We got this working for @robons17 and the long term fix landed. So i'm going to close this issue down. Please open a new issue if anyone else has a similar issue in future.

review_comments: I am wondering here if this should be the responsibility of the `zeroconf` integration or if `homekit_controller` should register with the zeroconf ServiceBrowser directly instead.
I think it's fine in this PR. Let's keep it.
